text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Commercial banks have raised interest rates after central bank moves to tighten monetary policy.
- More diversified financial instruments are the key to building up confidence in investment funds, a fund manager says.
- Banca Romana pentru Dezvoltare SA got a D rating from the international credit rating agency Moody's.
- Banca de Credit Popular SA launches a public subscription on Thursday to supplement its capital to the minimum level required by the central bank.
ADEVARUL
- Senate chairman Petre Roman said during a visit to Pitesti that the state budget deficit in 1996 accounted for 13 percent of the gross domestic product.
- Several bank managers will soon have to assume responsibility for irregularities in banking activities, police chief investigator Pavel Abraham says in an interview.
TINERETUL LIBER
- A delegation of Japan's Mitsubishi visited Romania looking into possibilities of cooperation with Romanian smelter Phoenix SA.
LIBERTATEA
- A family of four living on average wages spends 75 percent of their monthly incomes on food.
- Japan Credit Rating Agency representatives now in Bucharest met central bank governor Mugur Isarescu to discuss a new assessment for Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- Roman said the government had decided to look into the fulfilment of pledges made by South Korean company Daewoo when it entered the Romanian market. He said cooperation with Daewoo would be questioned if the difference between pledges and achievements proved unfavourable to Romania.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The national anti-corruption council, led by President Emil Constantinescu, drafted a programme for fighting mafia-like structures in oil and grain trading.

- Ex-president Ion Iliescu is on a list of 30 people who allegedly acquired their homes illegally, Valeriu Stan, head of the government's control body said. Stan said the houses were among state assets unavailable for sale.
ADEVARUL
- U.S. Assistant Secretary for European Affairs John Kornblum is expected to arrive in Bucharest on Saturday for a 24-hour visit, as part of a tour which includes Bosnia and Macedonia.
- Romania's chances to get NATO membership this year are 50 percent, says U.S.-based Romanian-born political analyst Vladimir Tismaneanu.

- IBM wants to connect all public administration institutions to the Internet, the company's president for Central and eastern Europe, Horst Breitenstein, said during a meeting with Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- Jews born in Romania will lobby for the country's early integration into NATO, said deputy Dorin Dorian, the representative of Romanian Jewish Communities.
- The Hungarian embassy in Strasbourg organised a reception in honour of the Romanian delegation at the Council of Europe's winter parliamentary session.
- Iliescu met Constantinescu and complained about the "political purging" since the centrist coalition took over, saying the cleansing affects local administration.
- A Bucharest Financial Guard officer was arrested after he was caught red handed taking bribes worth five million lei.
CURIERUL NATIONAL

- The former ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) has dropped its plan to complain to the Council of Europe about "political cleansing" by the centrist coalition, PDSR spokesman Teodor Melescanu said.
CRONICA ROMANA

- Greater Romania party leader Corneliu Vadim Tudor asked that coal miners' leader Miron Cosma be released to preserve "social peace". Cosma was arrested earlier this month pending investigations into riots led by miners in 1991.
- Romanian jails held some 88,500 prisoners in 1996, more than double their capacity of 30,300, report shows.
LIBERTATEA
- Some 16 percent of Romanians have all they want, while 39 percent say they have little or nothing of what they want, a survey published by the Central European Economic Review shows.
- A family with average monthly earnings needs to spend 75 percent of its income on food. ($= 5,778 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom at 40-1 3120264
